fixed.q: The most common type of business organisation is:
fixed.w: The sole proprietorship is the most common form of business.

fixed.q: ______ is also referred to as the Sales-Force-Composite method or the Collective Opinion Method.
fixed.w: The sales-force composite (collective opinion) method is a type of opinion survey.

fixed.q: What is effective desire?
fixed.w: Demand is effective desire: desire backed by willingness and ability to pay. The official key says 'Consumption', but the textbook answer is Demand. (The official key was wrong here; this is the corrected answer.)

fixed.q: ______ primarily deals with buying and selling, particularly on a large scale.
fixed.w: Commerce deals with buying and selling (trade and its aids) on a large scale.

fixed.q: Which of the following accounts is/are prepared for net profit?
o: Trading account, profit and loss account and balance sheet
fixed.w: The Profit and Loss account is prepared to find net profit.

fixed.q: A public company must have at least ______ members.
fixed.w: A public company needs at least 7 members.

fixed.q: Which of the following business structures has limited liability to its members?
fixed.w: A company gives its members limited liability.

fixed.q: According to business economics, the growth of an existing product is used to estimate the demand for a new product using:
fixed.w: The growth-curve approach estimates a new product's demand from the growth pattern of an existing product. The official key says 'substitute approach'. (The official key was wrong here; this is the corrected answer.)

fixed.q: Which method is used for demand forecasting of new products?
o: Evolutionary approach, opinion polling approach and vicarious approach
fixed.w: Demand for new products is forecast by the evolutionary, opinion-polling and vicarious approaches, among others (Joel Dean).

fixed.q: What is a long-term asset in accounting?
fixed.w: Fixed assets (property, plant, equipment) are long-term assets.

fixed.q: Which of the following is defined as that branch of economic analysis that studies the economic behaviour of the individual unit and may be a person, a particular household or a particular firm?
fixed.w: Microeconomics studies individual units such as a person, household or firm.

fixed.q: Which characteristic of business refers to 'various components of a business system are highly interacting and interdependent'?
fixed.w: Interdependence means the components of a business system interact with and depend on each other.

fixed.q: Which of the following is the proper sequence of the accounting cycle?
o: Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Adjusted Trial Balance → Closing Entries → Financial Statement
Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjusted Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Closing Entries → Financial Statement
Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Closing Entries → Adjusted Trial Balance → Financial Statement
Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Adjusted Trial Balance → Financial Statement → Closing Entries
fixed.w: The accounting cycle runs: transactions → journal → ledger → trial balance → adjustments → adjusted trial balance → closing entries → financial statements.

fixed.q: Which of the following refers to the art of recoding, classifying and summarising in a significant manner, and in terms of money, transactions and events that are in part at least of a financial character, and interpreting the results thereof?
fixed.w: This is the AICPA definition of (financial) accounting.

fixed.q: The ______ economic system is characterised by free markets and the absence of government intervention in the economy.
fixed.w: Capitalism means free markets and minimal government intervention.

fixed.q: Which of the following is the fundamental state of business activity and involves the sale and purchase of goods and services?
fixed.w: Trade (buying and selling goods and services) is the fundamental business activity.

fixed.q: The demand is said to be ______ when a very insignificant change in price leads to an infinite change in quantity demanded.
fixed.w: A tiny price change causing an infinite change in demand means perfectly elastic demand (a horizontal demand curve).

fixed.q: 'As the stock of a commodity increases with the consumer, its marginal utility to the consumer decreases'. To which of the following laws does the given statement refer?
fixed.w: This is the law of diminishing marginal utility.

fixed.q: Marginal revenue is calculated by ______.
o: dividing the change in total revenue by the change in total output quantity
dividing the change in total output quantity by the change in total revenue
dividing the change in total cost by the change in total output quantity
dividing the change in total revenue by the change in total profit
fixed.w: Marginal revenue = ΔTotal revenue ÷ ΔQuantity.

fixed.q: Any account or goods used by the owner of the business for his personal use is called as:
fixed.w: Cash or goods taken by the owner for personal use are drawings.

fixed.q: Elasticity of demand explains the ______ of the correlation between price and quantity.
fixed.w: Elasticity of demand measures the degree of responsiveness of quantity to price.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of business?
fixed.w: 'expense driven' is not a recognised type of business.

fixed.q: According to the double entry system, every transaction will have ______ entries.
fixed.w: Under double entry every transaction has a debit and a credit entry.

fixed.q: Which of the following inflations describes how demand for goods and services can drive up their prices?
fixed.w: Demand-pull inflation: excess demand pulls prices up.

fixed.q: An organisation structure establishes relationships between:
fixed.w: An organisation structure relates people, work and resources.

fixed.q: ______ is a person who carries on business by himself/herself.
fixed.w: A sole proprietor runs the business alone.

fixed.q: The part of the firm's capital that is required for conducting day-to-day expenses is called:
fixed.w: Working capital funds day-to-day operations.

fixed.q: An unhappy employee because of ______ processes in a business can negatively affect the corporate image of the business and make the business less successful.
fixed.w: Poor communication processes cause unhappy employees and hurt the corporate image.

fixed.q: Which of the following are the advantages of using the NEFT system? i) The transaction has legal backing. ii) Round the clock availability on all days of the year. iii) Near-real-time funds transfer to the beneficiary account and settlement in a secure manner. iv) Positive confirmation to the remitter by SMS/e-mail on credit to the beneficiary account.
o: i, ii, iii and iv only
fixed.w: NEFT transactions have legal backing, run 24×7, settle in near real time and confirm by SMS/e-mail. All four are advantages.

fixed.q: Which of the following are responsibilities of a Business Economist? i) Make a reasonable profit on capital employed. ii) Make successful forecasts by making in-depth study of the internal and external factors. iii) Inform the management of all the economic trends. iv) Establish and maintain contacts with individuals and data sources. v) Test and analyse the software.
o: i, ii, iii and iv only
fixed.w: A business economist earns a reasonable profit, forecasts, informs management of economic trends and maintains contacts; testing software is not their job.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are type(s) of business communication? i) Internal Business Communication ii) Lateral Business Communication iii) External Business Communication iv) Protected Business Communication
fixed.w: Internal, lateral and external are types of business communication; 'protected' is not.

fixed.q: Which of the following are the objectives of financial accounting? i) Proper recording of transactions ii) Ascertainment of the financial position iii) Reporting financial information iv) Defalcation prevention v) Digital marketing
o: i, ii, iii and iv only
fixed.w: Financial accounting covers recording, financial position, reporting and preventing fraud (defalcation); digital marketing is not part of it.

fixed.q: Which of the following are the dimensions of communication? i) Downward ii) Upward iii) Horizontal/Lateral iv) Diagonal v) Grapevine vi) Circular
o: i, ii, iii, iv and v
fixed.w: The dimensions are downward, upward, horizontal, diagonal and grapevine.

fixed.q: ______ is a discipline which deals with the application of economic theory to business management.
fixed.w: Business (managerial) economics applies economic theory to business management.

fixed.q: Which of the following are managerial functions? i) Planning ii) Organising iii) Staffing iv) Directing v) Controlling vi) Coding vii) Testing
o: i, ii, iii, iv and v only
i, ii, iii and iv only
fixed.w: The management functions are planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling.

fixed.q: ______ is a study of economics based on facts; it is verifiable, and you can prove or disprove it.
fixed.w: Positive economics is fact-based and verifiable; normative economics is value-based.

fixed.q: In a public limited company, the minimum number of shareholders is ______.
fixed.w: A public limited company needs at least seven members (Companies Act 2013); a private company needs two.

fixed.q: When the drawee fails to make the payment on the date of maturity, then a bill is said to have been ______.
fixed.w: A bill not paid on maturity is said to be dishonoured.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are the objective(s) of accounting? I. Maintenance of Records of Business Transactions II. Calculation of Profit and Loss
fixed.w: The objectives of accounting include maintaining records of transactions and calculating profit or loss. Both are objectives.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are the reason(s) for difference between cash book and bank passbook? I. Cheques paid into the bank but not yet collected II. Interest and dividends collected by the bank
fixed.w: Uncollected cheques and interest or dividends collected by the bank both cause differences between the cash book and the pass book.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding monopolistic competition?
o: The demand curve faced by the firm is horizontal
The market structure of the firm allows for new firms to enter the market
The marginal revenue is slightly less than the average revenue
The goods produced by them are not homogeneous
fixed.w: In monopolistic competition the demand curve slopes downward (it is elastic, not horizontal); only perfect competition has a horizontal demand curve.

fixed.q: Procedure for online trading involve(s) which of the following step(s)? I. Make an application to open a Demat Account and Online Trading Account. II. Allocate funds from the bank account to the trading account. III. Once the order is confirmed, it is placed in the stock exchange through the online trading system.
fixed.w: Online trading: open demat and trading accounts, transfer funds, then place orders that go to the exchange. All three steps.

fixed.q: Short run marginal cost curve is ______.
fixed.w: The short-run marginal cost curve is U-shaped (law of variable proportions).

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are the tool(s) of monetary policy of the RBI? I. Reverse Repo Rate II. Repo Rate III. Bank Rate
fixed.w: The repo rate, reverse repo rate and bank rate are all RBI monetary-policy tools.

fixed.q: A partner who just lends his name to the partnership firm is known as a ______.
fixed.w: A nominal partner only lends his name to the firm, without capital or management role.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are correct regarding accounting process? I. A provision is a charge against profit II. Reserve is an appropriation of profit
fixed.w: A provision is a charge against profit, while a reserve is an appropriation of profit. Both are true.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are correct? I. All permanent accounts are balanced and carried forward to the next accounting period. II. The temporary accounts are closed at the end of the accounting period.
fixed.w: Permanent (real) accounts are balanced and carried forward, while temporary (nominal) accounts are closed at period end. Both are true.

fixed.q: Which of the following effects of the price change can influence the consumer's optimal choice? I. The change in the relative price of a good. II. The change in the purchasing power of a consumer. III. Sudden reduction in the minimum support price of a commodity.
fixed.w: A price change acts through the substitution effect (relative price) and the income effect (purchasing power), so I and II.

fixed.q: A certain percentage of deposits which a bank must keep in the form of cash with the RBI is called ______.
fixed.w: The Cash Reserve Ratio is the share of deposits a bank must keep as cash with the RBI.

fixed.q: Which of the following method(s) is/are used to measure the aggregate value of goods and services produced in an economy? I. Expenditure method II. Income method III. Product method
fixed.w: GDP is measured by the expenditure, income and product (value-added) methods.

fixed.q: Under the Companies Act 2013, the maximum number of members in a private company is:
fixed.w: A private company: minimum 2, maximum 200 members (excluding present and past employee-members). A public company needs at least 7, with no maximum.

fixed.q: The minimum number of members needed to form a private limited company is:
fixed.w: Private company: minimum 2 members and 2 directors. Public: 7 members and 3 directors. One Person Company: 1.

fixed.q: A One Person Company (OPC) was introduced in India by:
fixed.w: The OPC was a new concept in the Companies Act 2013: a single member with limited liability.

fixed.q: Partnership firms in India are governed by:
fixed.w: Partnership firms come under the Indian Partnership Act 1932. LLPs come under the LLP Act 2008.

fixed.q: The liability of a sole proprietor is:
fixed.w: A sole proprietor and the business are the same legal person, so personal assets can be used to pay business debts.

fixed.q: In a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) business, the head of the family who manages it is called the:
fixed.w: The Karta (eldest member) manages the HUF business and has unlimited liability; the coparceners have liability limited to their share.

fixed.q: A cooperative society works mainly on the principle of:
fixed.w: Cooperatives exist to serve their members: one member, one vote; service rather than profit.

fixed.q: Which form of organisation has a separate legal entity and perpetual succession?
fixed.w: A company is an artificial legal person distinct from its members, so it continues even if members change or die (perpetual succession).

fixed.q: A partner who contributes capital and shares profits but does not take part in running the business is a:
fixed.w: A sleeping partner invests and shares profit but is not active. A nominal partner only lends his name.

fixed.q: Economic activities are classified into:
fixed.w: Economic activities are business, profession and employment. Business itself is divided into industry and commerce (trade plus aids to trade).

fixed.q: Banking, insurance, transport, warehousing and advertising are called:
fixed.w: Commerce = trade + aids to trade. These services remove hindrances of finance, risk, place, time and information.

fixed.q: POSDCORB, a list of management functions, was given by:
fixed.w: Gulick (1937): Planning, Organising, Staffing, Directing, Co-ordinating, Reporting, Budgeting.

fixed.q: The 14 principles of management were given by:
fixed.w: Fayol, the father of modern (administrative) management theory, gave the 14 principles such as unity of command and scalar chain.

fixed.q: "Father of Scientific Management" is:
fixed.w: Taylor introduced time study, motion study, differential piece-rate system and functional foremanship.

fixed.q: Management by Objectives (MBO) was introduced by:
fixed.w: Drucker introduced MBO in "The Practice of Management" (1954).

fixed.q: The first and most basic function of management is:
fixed.w: Planning comes first: deciding in advance what to do. Controlling is the last function and compares performance with plans.

fixed.q: The principle that an employee should receive orders from only one superior is:
fixed.w: Unity of command: one boss per employee. Unity of direction: one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective.

fixed.q: Maslow's need hierarchy in correct order from the bottom is:
fixed.w: Lowest are physiological needs; self-actualisation is at the top.

fixed.q: Communication from a manager to subordinates is called:
fixed.w: Downward: superior to subordinate. Upward: subordinate to superior. Horizontal (lateral): between people at the same level.

fixed.q: The informal channel of communication in an organisation is called the:
fixed.w: The grapevine is informal communication that spreads fast but can carry rumours.

fixed.q: The Law of Demand states that, other things remaining the same, when price rises, quantity demanded:
fixed.w: Price and quantity demanded are inversely related, so the demand curve slopes downward.

fixed.q: Price elasticity of demand is:
o: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price
% change in price ÷ % change in quantity demanded
Change in total revenue ÷ change in output
Change in price ÷ change in income
fixed.w: Ed = (%ΔQ)/(%ΔP). |Ed| > 1 elastic, < 1 inelastic, = 1 unitary, 0 perfectly inelastic, ∞ perfectly elastic.

fixed.q: When demand does not change at all in response to a change in price, demand is:
fixed.w: Perfectly inelastic: Ed = 0, the demand curve is vertical. Perfectly elastic: Ed = ∞, horizontal.

fixed.q: A market with a single seller and no close substitutes is:
fixed.w: Monopoly: one seller. Duopoly: two. Oligopoly: a few. Monopsony: one buyer.

fixed.q: Under perfect competition, the firm is a:
fixed.w: Many buyers and sellers of a homogeneous product, so a single firm cannot influence price and its demand curve is horizontal.

fixed.q: Total utility is maximum when marginal utility is:
fixed.w: Total utility keeps rising while MU is positive, peaks when MU = 0 and falls when MU becomes negative.

fixed.q: GDP can be measured by the:
o: Product (value added), income and expenditure methods
fixed.w: The three methods of measuring national income are the value-added (product), income and expenditure methods.

fixed.q: Inflation caused by a rise in production costs such as wages and raw materials is:
fixed.w: Cost-push: higher input costs push prices up. Demand-pull: excess demand pulls prices up.

fixed.q: Fiscal policy relates to:
fixed.w: Fiscal policy is the government's tax and spending policy (Ministry of Finance). Monetary policy is money supply and credit (RBI).

fixed.q: The cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run is:
fixed.w: Fixed costs (rent, salaries of permanent staff) stay the same whatever the output; variable costs change with output.

fixed.q: Opportunity cost means:
o: The value of the next best alternative given up
The total money cost of production
fixed.w: Opportunity cost is the benefit forgone from the best alternative not chosen.

fixed.q: The accounting equation is:
fixed.w: Every transaction keeps Assets = Liabilities + Owner's equity (capital) in balance.

fixed.q: Golden rule for a real account:
o: Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
Debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains
Debit the giver, credit the receiver
fixed.w: Real: debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Personal: debit the receiver, credit the giver. Nominal: debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains.

fixed.q: Golden rule for a nominal account:
o: Debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains
Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
Credit all expenses, debit all incomes
fixed.w: Nominal accounts (expenses, losses, incomes, gains) follow: debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains.

fixed.q: The book of original (prime) entry is the:
fixed.w: Transactions are first recorded in the journal, then posted to the ledger (the book of final entry).

fixed.q: A trial balance is prepared to check:
o: The arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts
The profit or loss of the business
The financial position of the business
fixed.w: A trial balance lists all ledger balances; if debit total = credit total, the books are arithmetically accurate (though some errors are not revealed).

fixed.q: A balance sheet shows:
o: The financial position of a business on a particular date
Cash received and paid during a year
fixed.w: The balance sheet is a statement of assets and liabilities on a date. The profit and loss account covers a period.

fixed.q: The concept that assumes a business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future is the:
fixed.w: Going concern: no intention to close, so assets are shown at cost less depreciation rather than at sale value.

fixed.q: The concept that the business is separate from its owner is the:
fixed.w: Business entity: owner and business are separate for accounting, so capital introduced by the owner is a liability of the business.

fixed.q: "Anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses" is the principle of:
fixed.w: Conservatism (prudence) means not recording expected gains but providing for expected losses.

fixed.q: Under the Straight Line Method (SLM), depreciation each year is:
o: A fixed percentage of the reducing balance
fixed.w: SLM: (Cost − Scrap value) ÷ Useful life every year. WDV: a fixed rate on the reducing book value, so the amount falls each year.

fixed.q: Expenditure on purchase of machinery is a:
fixed.w: Capital expenditure buys a long-term asset that benefits many years. Revenue expenditure (wages, repairs) benefits the current year.

fixed.q: Goods withdrawn by the owner for personal use are credited to the:
fixed.w: Entry: Drawings A/c Dr, To Purchases A/c, because those goods were bought for the business and are no longer available for sale.

fixed.q: Gross profit is calculated in the:
fixed.w: Trading account: Sales − Cost of goods sold = Gross profit. The profit and loss account then deducts indirect expenses to give net profit.

fixed.q: A Bank Reconciliation Statement is prepared by:
fixed.w: The business prepares a BRS to explain differences between its cash book (bank column) and the bank passbook.

fixed.q: RTGS transfers are settled:
o: Individually and in real time (gross basis)
Once a day after banking hours
fixed.w: RTGS = Real Time Gross Settlement: each transaction is settled one by one immediately, with a minimum of ₹2 lakh. NEFT settles in half-hourly batches.

fixed.q: The Negotiable Instruments Act was passed in:
fixed.w: The Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 covers promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques.

fixed.q: A cheque with two parallel transverse lines on its face is a:
fixed.w: Crossing means the cheque can only be paid into a bank account, not over the counter in cash.

fixed.q: The rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks is the:
fixed.w: Repo rate: RBI lends to banks against securities. Reverse repo: banks park money with the RBI. CRR and SLR are reserve ratios.

fixed.q: The portion of deposits that banks must keep as liquid assets (cash, gold, approved securities) with themselves is the:
fixed.w: SLR is kept with the bank itself. CRR is kept as cash with the RBI.

fixed.q: The market regulator for securities in India is:
fixed.w: SEBI (est. 1988, statutory in 1992) regulates the securities market. IRDAI regulates insurance.

fixed.q: The owners of a company are its:
fixed.w: Equity shareholders own the company. Debenture holders are its creditors and receive fixed interest.

fixed.q: Debentures represent the company's:
fixed.w: A debenture is an acknowledgement of debt; holders are creditors who get fixed interest.

fixed.q: Which of these is NOT a negotiable instrument under the NI Act 1881?
fixed.w: Under the NI Act the three negotiable instruments are promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques.

fixed.q: An IMPS transfer is available:
fixed.w: IMPS (run by NPCI) gives instant transfer at any time, every day of the year.

fixed.q: The "7 Cs" of effective business communication include:
fixed.w: The 7 Cs: clear, concise, concrete, correct, coherent, complete, courteous (some lists use consideration).

fixed.q: A memo (memorandum) is mainly used for:
fixed.w: Memos are short internal messages; letters go to outside parties.

fixed.q: The written record of the proceedings of a meeting is called the:
fixed.w: The agenda lists items before the meeting; the minutes record decisions after it; a quorum is the minimum attendance.

fixed.q: In a business letter, the "salutation" is:
fixed.w: Salutation opens the letter; the complimentary close (Yours faithfully/sincerely) ends it.

fixed.q: Noise, jargon and emotional bias are examples of:
fixed.w: Barriers can be physical, semantic (language), psychological or organisational.

fixed.q: Report writing usually begins with an executive summary because it:
o: Gives busy readers the key findings and recommendations quickly
Is required only in legal documents
fixed.w: The executive summary condenses the purpose, findings and recommendations.

theory.Business organisation:
• Economic activities: business, profession, employment. Business = industry + commerce; commerce = trade + aids to trade (banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, advertising).
• Sole proprietorship: most common, one owner, unlimited liability, no separate entity.
• Partnership: Indian Partnership Act 1932; partners' liability unlimited. Types of partner: active, sleeping (dormant: capital, no work), nominal (name only), partner by estoppel. LLP: LLP Act 2008, limited liability.
• HUF: Karta manages it (unlimited liability); coparceners have limited liability.
• Cooperative: service motive, one member one vote.
• Company (Companies Act 2013): separate legal entity, limited liability, perpetual succession, common seal. Private: 2–200 members, 2 directors. Public: min 7 members, 3 directors. OPC: 1 member.
theory.Management & communication:
• Fayol: 14 principles (division of work, authority & responsibility, discipline, unity of command, unity of direction, subordination of individual interest, remuneration, centralisation, scalar chain, order, equity, stability of tenure, initiative, esprit de corps).
• Taylor: scientific management, time & motion study, differential piece rate, functional foremanship.
• Gulick: POSDCORB. Drucker: MBO. Maslow: need hierarchy. McGregor: Theory X/Y. Herzberg: two-factor theory.
• Functions: planning (first), organising, staffing, directing, controlling (last).
• Communication: downward, upward, horizontal (lateral), diagonal; formal vs informal (grapevine).
theory.Economics:
• Micro (individual units: consumer, firm) vs macro (economy: GDP, inflation). Positive (what is, verifiable) vs normative (what ought to be).
• Law of demand: price ↑ → quantity demanded ↓. Demand = desire + ability + willingness to pay (effective desire).
• Elasticity Ed = %ΔQ/%ΔP: perfectly elastic ∞ (horizontal), perfectly inelastic 0 (vertical), unitary 1.
• Law of diminishing marginal utility; total utility maximum when MU = 0.
• Markets: perfect competition (price taker), monopoly (one seller), duopoly, oligopoly (few), monopolistic competition (product differentiation, downward-sloping demand).
• Costs: fixed vs variable; short-run MC, AC are U-shaped. MR = ΔTR/ΔQ.
• National income: product/value-added, income and expenditure methods.
• Inflation: demand-pull vs cost-push. Fiscal policy = taxes and spending (government); monetary policy = money and credit (RBI).
• Economic systems: capitalist (free market), socialist (state), mixed (India).
• Demand forecasting: survey of buyers' intentions, collective opinion (sales-force composite), expert opinion (Delphi), trend projection; new products: evolutionary, substitute, growth curve, opinion polling, sales experience, vicarious approach.
theory.Accounting:
• Accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Double entry: every transaction has a debit and a credit.
• Golden rules: Personal – debit receiver, credit giver. Real – debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Nominal – debit expenses/losses, credit incomes/gains.
• Cycle: transaction → journal (book of original entry) → ledger (final entry) → trial balance (arithmetical accuracy) → final accounts.
• Final accounts: Trading A/c (gross profit), Profit & Loss A/c (net profit), Balance Sheet (position on a date).
• Concepts: business entity, going concern, money measurement, accrual, matching, dual aspect, conservatism (prudence), consistency, materiality.
• Depreciation: SLM (equal every year) vs WDV (fixed % of reducing balance).
• Capital expenditure (long-term asset) vs revenue expenditure (current year). Drawings: owner's personal use.
• Working capital = current assets − current liabilities. BRS reconciles cash book with passbook.
• Bill of exchange dishonoured when the drawee fails to pay on maturity.
theory.Banking & finance:
• RBI tools: repo (RBI lends to banks), reverse repo (banks park with RBI), CRR (cash kept with RBI), SLR (liquid assets kept by bank), bank rate, OMO, MSF.
• Payments: NEFT (half-hourly batches, 24×7), RTGS (real-time gross, min ₹2 lakh), IMPS (instant, 24×7, NPCI), UPI (NPCI).
• Negotiable Instruments Act 1881: promissory note, bill of exchange, cheque. Crossed cheque: only into an account.
• Shares (ownership; equity holders own the company) vs debentures (loan; holders are creditors, fixed interest).
• SEBI regulates securities (statutory 1992). IRDAI insurance. NABARD rural credit.
• Online trading: Demat account + trading account with a broker, then place orders.
